When_Not_To_Apply: When your product doesn't need cloud (static site on Vercel is fine)
Warning: Don't apply for $100K AWS credits just to use $50/month

When_Not_To_Apply: When you're not using GCP services or Kubernetes
Warning: Switching from AWS to GCP just for credits = migration overhead

When_Not_To_Apply: When you're not building B2B or enterprise product
Warning: Azure has steeper learning curve for solo devs vs Supabase/Vercel

When_Not_To_Apply: When you need managed services (auth/realtime/edge functions)
Warning: DigitalOcean is raw — you'll need to configure everything yourself

When_Not_To_Apply: Stage 0-2: Don't set up product analytics before having users
Warning: Configuring 50 events with 0 users = wasted week

When_Not_To_Apply: Stage 0-3: CDP is overkill before you have multiple data sources
Warning: Segment adds value when you have 3+ analytics tools — not before

When_Not_To_Apply: Stage 0-2: Don't add chat widget to site with 0 visitors
Warning: Intercom is expensive after year 1 — have revenue first
Zendesk adds complexity for low-volume support. Use Gmail labels

When_Not_To_Apply: Stage 0-2: CRM is premature when you have 0 leads
Warning: HubSpot is powerful but heavy — consider lighter CRM first

When_Not_To_Apply: When you have flat/simple pricing (use Stripe Checkout directly)
Warning: Chargebee adds value for complex billing — simple pricing doesn't need it

When_Not_To_Apply: When solo founder — free personal plan is usually sufficient
Warning: Don't get team plan credits when it's just you

When_Not_To_Apply: When you're not using Next.js or React frameworks
Warning: Vercel is optimized for Next.js — other frameworks may not benefit

When_Not_To_Apply: When you're not planning to operate in the US market
Warning: Delaware C-Corp adds tax complexity for non-US founders
